title: The Year of One Bed at a Time
opening: Pat started the year asking how a vegetable bed works and finished it with a planner that gets used every week. The middle was messier than that. This is an invented example.

chapters.title: Asking before digging
text: Most of the winter was questions about soil, frost dates and what grows next to what. Only the typed prompts survive, so this part is a sketch.

chapters.title: The planner that planned everything
text: April's planner covered every bed, every season and the compost. It was never finished.
In May Pat threw it out and built a planner for one bed. That one was done in a weekend.
chapters.changed: Pat began starting with the smallest version that would be useful on its own.

chapters.title: Water, then quiet
text: June was the pond and a lot of arithmetic about liners. No records survive for July.

chapters.title: Making it for other people
text: The garden club asked for a newsletter, and the template from August produced the first issue two days into September.
By October the same habit had reached the recipes.
chapters.changed: Work started going to other people, so it had to be clear enough to hand over.

worked.claim: Building one bed first got the planner finished.
A template made the newsletter quick.

didnt.claim: Planning every bed at once stalled for a month.
Winter questions were asked more than once, because the answers weren't kept.

carry: Write answers down where they will be found.
Finish the small version before drawing the big one.
